w.label: 01 · Introduction
w.head: Catch the reader
steps: Engage the reader and name it
Introduce it — what it is known for

w.label: 01 · Introduction
w.head: Catch the reader
ex: Choosing a … can be a real challenge; however, … is certainly an option worth considering.
Known for its …, it has been a favourite among …
rows: {Choosing a} café {can be a real challenge; however,} <Café Azul> {is certainly an option worth considering.}
{Known for its} homemade cakes, {it has been a favourite among} teenagers for years.

w.label: 01 · Introduction
w.head: Catch the reader
ex: When it comes to …, few options can compete with …
Located in …, it remains an emblematic …
rows: {When it comes to} cafés, {few options can compete with} <Café Azul>.
{Located in} the old town, {it remains an emblematic} meeting place for locals and tourists.

w.label: 01 · Introduction
w.head: Catch the reader
ex: If you are looking for a …, then … could be the perfect option for you.
Regarded as one of the best …
rows: Two in one sentence
{If you are looking for a} relaxing café, {then} <Café Azul>, {regarded as one of the best}, {could be the perfect option for you.}

w.label: 02 · Features
w.head: Name it · carry it on
steps: One feature in each paragraph
Name the feature
Carry it on: a reason, an example, or a small drawback

w.label: 02 · Features
w.head: Name it · carry it on
rows: {What impressed me most was} the food, which is absolutely mouth-watering.
Reason
_This is because_ everything is made fresh every morning.

w.label: 02 · Features
w.head: Name it · carry it on
ex: If you happen to appreciate …, … is by far the most … I have …
rows: {If you happen to appreciate} good coffee, their espresso {is by far the most} delicious {I have} tasted.
Example
_For instance,_ even a simple cup feels like a treat there.

w.label: 02 · Features
w.head: Name it · carry it on
ex: By far the most appealing aspect of … is …
rows: Feature + drawback in one sentence
{By far the most appealing aspect of} <Café Azul> {is} its sunny terrace overlooking the harbour, _although_ it can get quite crowded at weekends.

w.label: 03 · Recommendation
w.head: Should I try it?
steps: Recommend it
Say who will enjoy it most
Add nothing new

w.label: 03 · Recommendation
w.head: Should I try it?
ex: This is a … which you cannot afford to miss for its …
rows: {This is a} café {which you cannot afford to miss for its} homemade cakes.
Who it suits
It is ideal for students looking for a quiet place to relax.

w.label: 03 · Recommendation
w.head: Should I try it?
ex: For anyone who is interested in …, … is a must.
rows: {For anyone who is interested in} good coffee, <Café Azul> {is a must.}
Who it suits
It is perfect for a relaxed afternoon with friends.

w.label: 03 · Recommendation
w.head: Should I try it?
ex: I can assure you that … will leave a lasting impression on you.
rows: The whole review in one sentence
{I can assure you that} <Café Azul>, with its delicious cakes and sunny terrace, {will leave a lasting impression on you,} whether you are a local or just visiting.

scenes.sub: Try these expressions on the cards.

scenes.q: Some people say tourism does more harm than good. Do you agree?

w.label: 01 · Introduction
w.head: Set the scene
steps: Set the scene with a general statement
Say what the essay will do

w.label: 01 · Introduction
w.head: Set the scene
ex: There has been a growing recognition that …
Consequently, I will explain why I agree / disagree with this statement.
rows: {There has been a growing recognition that} <tourism> can damage the places people love to visit.
{Consequently, I will explain why I} disagree {with this statement.}

w.label: 01 · Introduction
w.head: Set the scene
ex: It is a well-established fact that …
Hence, I would like to present my views on …
rows: {It is a well-established fact that} <tourism> is one of the largest industries in the world.
{Hence, I would like to present my views on} whether it does more harm than good.

w.label: 01 · Introduction
w.head: Set the scene
ex: Over the past few years, there has been a significant increase in …
… it is important to examine the arguments both for and against …
rows: Two in one sentence
{Over the past few years, there has been a significant increase in} <tourism>, which is why {it is important to examine the arguments both for and against} it.

w.label: 02 · Arguments
w.head: Argue · support it
steps: One argument in each paragraph — use the notes
Introduce the argument
Support it: a reason or an example

w.label: 02 · Arguments
w.head: Argue · support it
ex: One strong argument in favour of … is that it …
rows: {One strong argument in favour of} <tourism> {is that it} creates jobs for millions of people.
Reason
_This is because_ hotels, restaurants and shops all need staff.

w.label: 02 · Arguments
w.head: Argue · support it
ex: On the other hand, a key argument against … is that it negatively affects …
rows: {On the other hand, a key argument against} <tourism> {is that it negatively affects} the environment.
Example
_For example,_ popular beaches are often left full of rubbish.

w.label: 02 · Arguments
w.head: Argue · support it
ex: It is often claimed that … helps to …
rows: Your own idea — both sides in one sentence
{It is often claimed that} <tourism> {helps to} protect local traditions, _although_ {critics argue that} it can also turn them into a show for visitors.

w.label: 03 · Conclusion
w.head: Your opinion
steps: Give your opinion clearly
Sum up both sides — say which is stronger
Add nothing new

w.label: 03 · Conclusion
w.head: Your opinion
ex: On balance, it appears that … brings more advantages than disadvantages.
rows: {On balance, it appears that} <tourism> {brings more advantages than disadvantages.}
Balance
_However,_ it must be managed carefully.

w.label: 03 · Conclusion
w.head: Your opinion
ex: In conclusion, although there are strong arguments on both sides, I firmly believe that …
rows: {In conclusion, although there are strong arguments on both sides, I firmly believe that} <tourism> does more good than harm.

w.label: 03 · Conclusion
w.head: Your opinion
ex: To sum up, while … has both supporters and critics, the evidence strongly supports …
rows: Add a condition
{To sum up, while} <tourism> {has both supporters and critics, the evidence strongly supports} it, _provided that_ visitors respect the places they explore.

scenes.sub: Try these expressions on the cards.

scenes.q: Your head teacher wants to improve the school canteen and has asked you for a report.

w.label: 01 · Introduction
w.head: Aim · source
steps: Say what the report is for
Say where the information comes from

w.label: 01 · Introduction
w.head: Aim · source
ex: The purpose of this report is to examine …
The information in this report was collected through a survey among …
rows: {The purpose of this report is to examine} how students feel about <the school canteen>.
{The information in this report was collected through a survey among} two hundred students.

w.label: 01 · Introduction
w.head: Aim · source
ex: This report aims to provide a summary of …
The findings in this report are drawn from interviews and feedback during …
rows: {This report aims to provide a summary of} students' views on <the canteen>.
{The findings in this report are drawn from interviews and feedback during} lunch breaks last month.

w.label: 01 · Introduction
w.head: Aim · source
ex: The main objective of this report is to assess …
rows: Two in one sentence
{The main objective of this report is to assess} <the school canteen>, {based on a questionnaire} completed by students in every year group.

w.label: 02 · Findings
w.head: What people said
steps: Present the findings under headings
Sum up what people said
Support it with a reason or a detail

w.label: 02 · Findings
w.head: What people said
ex: By far the best aspect of … is that …
Many … referred to … as the best part of …
rows: {By far the best aspect of} <the canteen> {is that} meals are freshly cooked every day.
Detail
{Many} students {referred to} the pasta {as the best part of} the week.

w.label: 02 · Findings
w.head: What people said
ex: One major concern expressed by … is …
This is mainly due to the fact that …
rows: {One major concern expressed by} students {is} the length of the queues.
Reason
_This is mainly due to the fact that_ only one counter is open at lunchtime.

w.label: 02 · Findings
w.head: What people said
rows: Finding + reason in one sentence
{It was generally felt that} the menu is too repetitive, _considering that_ the same dishes appear every week.

w.label: 03 · Recommendations
w.head: What should change
steps: Recommend clear, practical changes
Draw a conclusion
Add no new findings

w.label: 03 · Recommendations
w.head: What should change
ex: In order to …, I would strongly recommend …
rows: {In order to} reduce the queues, {I would strongly recommend} opening a second counter.
Result
This would save students at least ten minutes every day.

w.label: 03 · Recommendations
w.head: What should change
ex: To sum up, the findings clearly show that …
rows: {To sum up, the findings clearly show that} students value <the canteen>, but they would like more variety.

w.label: 03 · Recommendations
w.head: What should change
ex: Taking everything into account, it seems clear that …
… one key recommendation would be to …
rows: Conclusion + recommendation in one sentence
{Taking everything into account, it seems clear that} <the canteen> is popular, but {one key recommendation would be to} offer a wider choice of dishes.
